parole.significato: sign marking the boundary of a sown land, usually made out of twigs or straws; furrow
parole.testo: Cognate with Proto-Slavic *borzda and Latvian bìrze (“furrow”). Possibly derived from Proto-Indo-European *bʰers- (“top, point”) or from Proto-Indo-European *bʰerH- (“to bore a hole”), see the Proto-Slavic form for more.

parole.significato: receipt (an official certificate showing the delivery and receipt of money and other valuables)
parole.testo: Probably borrowed from Polish kwit, ultimately from Middle High German quit-brief. Compare Latvian kvīts, which may have come from either Polish or directly from Baltic German, and more distant Russian квита́нция (kvitáncija).
Borrowed from Germanic, either from Gothic *midus (“mead”) or German Met (“id”). Doublet of medùs.
